item.title: AI and the ironies of automation – Part 2
item.description:
📝 The usual idea is that a single human controls a fleet of AI agents that are designed to do some kind of job, e. Sometimes, most agents are generic “workers”, orchestrated by some kind of supervisor that delegates parts of the work to the worker agents. Therefore, the AI agents typically create a plan of what they intend to do first (which as a side effect also increases the likelihood that they do not drift off).
🔗 Read more: https://www.ufried.com/blog/ironies_of_ai_2/

item.title: Efficient Basic Coding for the ZX Spectrum
item.description:
📝 A la hora de editar manualmente un programa sólo se nos permite numerar las líneas desde 1 a 9999. La longitud en bytes de cada línea de programa se almacena justo después del número de línea, ocupando 2 bytes (esta vez en little-endian). Esta longitud no incluye ni el número de línea ni la longitud en sí misma.
🔗 Read more: https://blog.jafma.net/2020/02/24/efficient-basic-coding-for-the-zx-spectrum/

item.title: Baumol's Cost Disease
item.description:
📝 Some sectors experience high productivity growth, while others experience little or negative productivity growth. [8] Yet wages have tended to rise not only in sectors with high productivity growth, but also in those with little to no productivity growth. With higher labor costs, but little increase in productivity, sectors with low productivity growth see their costs of production rise.
🔗 Read more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baumol_effect
